title: Dynamics
description: Dynamics develops the ability to model and predict the motion of particles, systems of particles, and rigid bodies under applied forces and moments. Students move among kinematics, Newton-Euler equations, work-energy, impulse-momentum, and angular-momentum methods. They choose coordinates and system boundaries deliberately and verify results using dimensional, limiting-case, graphical, and computational checks. The shared core serves general, mechanical, civil, and aerospace engineering, with applications tailored by discipline rather than separate syllabi.

resources.title: Engineering Mechanics: Dynamics (Hibbeler)
resources.description: R. C. Hibbeler. Highly structured undergraduate treatment with abundant particle and rigid-body examples and graded problem sets.

resources.title: Engineering Mechanics: Dynamics (Meriam, Kraige, and Bolton)
resources.description: Rigorous vector mechanics, strong diagrams, and broad engineering applications. Used in current Georgia Tech syllabi.

resources.title: Vector Mechanics for Engineers: Dynamics
resources.description: Beer, Johnston, Cornwell, and Self. Systematic vector approach with strong coverage of kinematics, kinetics, energy, momentum, and rigid bodies.

resources.title: Introduction to Statics and Dynamics
resources.description: Ruina and Pratap. Free, conceptually careful mechanics reference with modeling insight and challenging problems.

resources.title: Advanced Engineering Dynamics
resources.description: Jerry Ginsberg. Instructor enrichment for spatial motion, analytical mechanics, and later dynamics courses.

resources.title: Mechanical Vibrations / Engineering Vibration
resources.description: Rao and Inman. Deeper SDOF, MDOF, modal, isolation, and vibration-design treatment beyond the final course unit.

resources.title: MIT OCW 2.003SC Engineering Dynamics
resources.description: Lectures, demonstrations, problem sets, videos, and a benchmark sequence spanning rigid-body dynamics and vibration.

resources.title: MIT OCW 2.003J Dynamics and Control I
resources.description: Computational and analytical extension through Lagrange equations, stability, and multi-degree vibration.

resources.title: Mechanics Map
resources.description: Visual explanations and worked engineering mechanics examples.

resources.title: Engineering LibreTexts - Dynamics
resources.description: Accessible chapters and examples for review and alternative explanations.

resources.title: MATLAB and Simulink
resources.description: Numerical ODE solutions, parameter sweeps, animation, signal analysis, and vibration response.

resources.title: Python: NumPy, SciPy, SymPy, Matplotlib
resources.description: Reproducible numerical integration, symbolic checks, plotting, and parameter studies without license cost.

resources.title: Jeff Hanson
resources.description: Clear worked examples in statics, dynamics, mechanics of materials, and vibrations.

resources.title: ASME Dynamic Systems and Control Division
resources.description: Professional bridge to dynamics, controls, mechatronics, vibration, and system design.

resources.title: NASA Technical Reports Server and ASCE Structural Engineering Institute

topics.title: Vector Mechanics Review and Modeling Workflow
topics.description: This opening unit prepares students to translate physical motion into solvable engineering models. It keeps the course grounded in diagrams, units, coordinates, and assumptions before equations appear.

children.title: Vectors and components
children.description: Students review how to represent motion, force, and moment quantities in component form. The point is to make geometry computationally reliable.

children.title: Free-body and kinetic diagrams
children.description: Dynamics problems require both the forces on a body and the motion response. Students learn to pair free-body diagrams with acceleration or kinetic diagrams.

children.title: Modeling assumptions
children.description: Students learn to simplify without hiding the physics. The gist is to state what is ignored and why the model remains useful.

children.title: Problem-solving workflow
children.description: Students learn a repeatable method for dynamics problems. This reduces algebra drift and helps catch impossible answers.

topics.title: Particle Kinematics: Rectilinear and Curvilinear Motion
topics.description: This unit studies motion without yet asking what caused it. Students learn to describe position, velocity, and acceleration accurately in one, two, and three dimensions.

children.title: Rectilinear motion
children.description: Students learn motion along a straight line. The gist is to connect displacement, velocity, and acceleration through calculus and graphs.

children.title: Curvilinear motion
children.description: Students learn how motion along a curved path differs from straight-line motion. Acceleration can exist even at constant speed because direction changes.

children.title: Motion graphs
children.description: Graphs reveal relationships that equations can hide. Students learn to interpret slopes and areas physically.

children.title: Projectile and path motion
children.description: Students apply kinematics to common engineering examples. The point is to practice decomposition into independent directions.

topics.title: Coordinate Systems and Relative Motion of Particles
topics.description: This unit teaches students to choose coordinates that fit the motion. Good coordinate choices make hard problems much cleaner.

children.title: Normal-tangential coordinates
children.description: Students learn to describe motion along a known path. This is especially useful for vehicles, cams, and curved guides.

children.title: Polar and cylindrical coordinates
children.description: Students learn motion described by radial and angular variables. The gist is that unit vectors can change direction over time.

children.title: Relative motion
children.description: Students learn to describe one particle's motion as observed from another. This supports pursuit, linkages, and moving-frame problems.

children.title: Constrained motion
children.description: Students practice motion relationships created by cables, pulleys, sliders, and mechanisms.

topics.title: Particle Kinetics Using Newton's Laws
topics.description: This unit introduces force as the cause of acceleration. Students learn to connect free-body diagrams directly to equations of motion.

children.title: Newton's second law
children.description: Students use F = ma as the core force-acceleration relationship. The point is to write equations in directions aligned with the motion.

children.title: Rectangular and path-coordinate kinetics
children.description: Students learn that the same law can be written in different coordinate systems. The best choice depends on the motion.

children.title: Friction and contact forces
children.description: Students include real interaction forces in motion problems. The gist is to distinguish normal reactions from resistance forces.

children.title: Applications
children.description: Students apply Newton's laws to common systems. This builds fluency in setup, not just computation.

topics.title: Work-Energy Methods for Particles
topics.description: Work-energy methods offer an efficient alternative when displacement and speed matter more than time. Students learn to solve motion problems without always tracking acceleration histories.

children.title: Work of a force
children.description: Students learn how forces transfer energy through displacement. The gist is that only the component along motion does work.

children.title: Kinetic energy
children.description: Students connect mass and speed to energy of motion.

children.title: Principle of work and energy
children.description: Students learn a compact equation for relating initial and final states.

children.title: Conservative forces and potential energy
children.description: Students learn when energy can be stored and recovered. This sets up conservation methods.

topics.title: Impulse, Momentum, and Impact for Particles
topics.description: Momentum methods are strongest when forces act over time, especially during collisions or short impulses. Students learn to analyze interactions where acceleration is hard to model directly.

children.title: Linear impulse and momentum
children.description: Students learn the time-integral form of Newton's second law. The point is to relate force duration to velocity change.

children.title: Conservation of momentum
children.description: Students learn when total momentum remains constant for a system. This is essential for collisions and explosions.

children.title: Impact
children.description: Students model collisions using momentum and restitution. The gist is to handle short-duration contact without detailed deformation analysis.

children.title: Angular momentum of a particle
children.description: Students learn momentum about a point, which prepares them for rigid-body dynamics.

topics.title: Systems of Particles and Center-of-Mass Methods
topics.description: This unit moves from one particle to many. Students learn how aggregate motion can be simpler than tracking every internal interaction.

children.title: Center of mass
children.description: Students learn the representative point for a mass distribution. The gist is that external forces drive center-of-mass motion.

children.title: System linear momentum
children.description: Students extend momentum methods to multiple bodies. This supports vehicle, projectile, and collision systems.

children.title: System work-energy
children.description: Students learn how energy methods apply to interacting particles.

children.title: Applications
children.description: Students use system methods where individual-body equations are messy.

topics.title: Rigid Body Kinematics: Translation, Rotation, and General Plane Motion
topics.description: Rigid bodies have both motion of a reference point and rotation about that point. Students learn to describe motion of every point on a body consistently.

children.title: Translation and fixed-axis rotation
children.description: Students learn the two simplest rigid-body motions. These create the foundation for wheels, gears, shafts, and mechanisms.

children.title: General plane motion
children.description: Students learn the combination of translation and rotation in a plane. The gist is that a body's points can have different velocities and accelerations.

children.title: Instantaneous center of zero velocity
children.description: Students learn a graphical and conceptual shortcut for planar velocity analysis.

children.title: Mechanism kinematics
children.description: Students apply rigid-body kinematics to connected parts.

topics.title: Rigid Body Kinetics: Force-Acceleration and Moment Equations
topics.description: This unit connects forces and moments to rigid-body acceleration. Students learn that rotation requires moment equations in addition to force equations.

children.title: Mass moments of inertia
children.description: Students learn the rotational measure of mass distribution. The gist is that the same mass can be easy or hard to spin depending on its distribution.

children.title: Planar equations of motion
children.description: Students learn the core rigid-body kinetics equations.

children.title: Sum of forces equals mass times acceleration
Sum of moments equals I alpha
Rolling and contact
children.description: Students analyze bodies that translate and rotate together.

children.title: Dynamic equilibrium form
children.description: Students learn an alternative bookkeeping method using inertia forces and inertia moments.

topics.title: Work-Energy and Impulse-Momentum Methods for Rigid Bodies
topics.description: This unit extends efficient energy and momentum tools to rotating bodies. Students learn when scalar energy equations or momentum balances are faster than force-acceleration equations.

children.title: Rigid-body kinetic energy
children.description: Students learn to combine translational and rotational kinetic energy.

children.title: Work-energy for rigid bodies
children.description: Students solve rigid-body speed and displacement problems without tracking all accelerations.

children.title: Angular impulse-momentum
children.description: Students learn how moments acting over time change angular momentum.

children.title: Applications
children.description: Students practice choosing between force-acceleration, energy, and momentum methods.

topics.title: Rotating Reference Frames and Three-Dimensional Dynamics
topics.description: This advanced core unit handles motion seen from moving or rotating frames and spatial motion. It is especially important for aerospace, mechanical systems, and rotating machinery.

children.title: Relative motion in rotating frames
children.description: Students learn why extra acceleration terms appear in rotating coordinates.

children.title: Coriolis and centripetal effects
children.description: Students learn to identify acceleration terms caused by rotation of the observer frame.

children.title: Three-dimensional rigid-body kinematics
children.description: Students learn how angular velocity and angular acceleration behave as vectors in space.

children.title: Three-dimensional kinetics
children.description: Students get an introductory view of moments and inertia in 3D.

topics.title: Mechanical Vibrations and Introductory System Dynamics
topics.description: The final unit introduces dynamic response over time. Students learn how mass, stiffness, damping, and forcing create oscillatory behavior in machines and structures.

children.title: Single-degree-of-freedom models
children.description: Students learn the simplest model for vibration analysis. The gist is to reduce a physical system to mass, spring, and damper elements.

children.title: Free vibration and damping
children.description: Students learn how systems oscillate after an initial disturbance.

children.title: Underdamped, critically damped, and overdamped cases
Forced vibration
children.description: Students learn how systems respond to external harmonic input. This explains resonance and many engineering design constraints.

children.title: Introductory modal and experimental ideas
children.description: Students see the bridge to graduate Dynamics and Vibrations.
